## Overview

Unlike parsimony or time-homogeneous Mk2 trait models, the **Volz (2012) structured coalescent** relates branch coalescent and migration hazards directly to the time-varying epidemiological birth matrix $F(t)$, migration matrix $G(t)$, and deme prevalences $Y(t)$.

`Phylodynamics.jl` provides a complete suite of structured coalescent likelihood and ancestral state reconstruction tools:

- **`DatedTree(tree; demes, sampleTimes, sampleStates)`**: Constructs a dated genealogy with tip state probability annotations.
- **`build_demographic_process(rs, infected, u0, tspan, p)`**: Builds a callable demographic process `dm(theta, x0, t0, t1; res)` directly from a `ModelingToolkit.ReactionSystem`.
- **`colik(bdt, theta, dm; likelihood = :PL2 | :PL1 | :QL)`**: Evaluates the structured coalescent log-likelihood using any of the three lineage-state integration approximations (`solvePikL1`, `solvePikL0`, or `solveQAL`).
- **`ace(bdt, theta, dm)`**: Performs forward-backward Ancestral Character Estimation (`solveQfwd0`) to compute posterior deme probabilities at all internal nodes.
- **`island_coalescent_ml(tree; ...)`**, **`confint_island_coalescent`**, and **`boot_island_coalescent`**: Fits an equilibrium constant-population structured coalescent island model.

## Building a demographic process from a `ReactionSystem`

```{julia}
using Phylodynamics
using Phylodynamics.Zoonosis
using ModelingToolkit
using Catalyst
using CairoMakie
using DataFrames
using StableRNGs
using Printf

bundle = build_zoonosis_reaction_system()
sp = bundle.species
pr = bundle.params
zp2 = model2_params()

u0 = [sp.X1 => zp2.X1_0, sp.Y1 => zp2.Y1_0, sp.X2 => zp2.X2_0, sp.Y2 => zp2.Y2_0]
p  = [pr.nu1 => zp2.nu1, pr.mu1 => zp2.mu1, pr.gamma1 => zp2.gamma1, pr.m1 => zp2.m1,
      pr.beta => zp2.beta, pr.nu2 => zp2.nu2, pr.mu2 => zp2.mu2, pr.gamma2 => zp2.gamma2,
      pr.m2 => zp2.m2, pr.epsilon => zp2.epsilon, pr.phi => zp2.phi, pr.psi => zp2.psi]

dm = build_demographic_process(bundle.rs, [sp.Y1, sp.Y2], u0, (0.0, zp2.t_peak), p)
```

Given a simulated phylogeny `t2`, we wrap it in a `DatedTree` and compare the `:PL2`, `:PL1`, and `:QL` likelihood approximations of `colik`:

```{julia}
t1 = simulate_coalescent_tree(model1_params(); n1 = 100, n2 = 10, rng = StableRNG(101))
t2 = simulate_coalescent_tree(model2_params(); n1 = 100, n2 = 10, rng = StableRNG(202))
t3 = simulate_coalescent_tree(model3_params(); n1 = 100, n2 = 30, rng = StableRNG(42))

bdt2 = DatedTree(t2; demes = ["Y1", "Y2"], minEdgeLength = 1e-5)
theta_true = Dict("epsilon" => 0.01, "phi" => 4.0, "psi" => 0.0)

DataFrame(
    Approximation = [":PL2 (solvePikL1)", ":PL1 (solvePikL0)", ":QL (solveQAL)"],
    LogLikelihood = [
        colik(bdt2, theta_true, dm; res = 300, timeOfOriginBoundaryCondition = false, likelihood = :PL2),
        colik(bdt2, theta_true, dm; res = 300, timeOfOriginBoundaryCondition = false, likelihood = :PL1),
        colik(bdt2, theta_true, dm; res = 300, timeOfOriginBoundaryCondition = false, likelihood = :QL)
    ]
)
```

## Profile likelihoods and hypothesis tests for $\phi$ (human spread) and $\psi$ (reverse zoonosis)

Using `profile_structured_coalescent(t1, t2, t3)`, we compute likelihood slices over the human-to-human transmission multiplier $\phi$ (comparing $H_0: \phi = 0$), the reverse zoonosis multiplier $\psi$ (comparing $H_0: \psi = 0$), and the 2D $(\epsilon, \phi)$ surface. Other parameters remain fixed at their generating values; these are not nuisance-parameter-optimized profile likelihoods:

```{julia}
prof = profile_structured_coalescent(t1, t2, t3; likelihood = :PL2)
fig_prof = plot_fig7_structured_coalescent_profiles(prof; outdir = mktempdir())
fig_prof
```

The following table computes the grid maxima and likelihood differences from
these simulated trees, rather than assuming that each maximum equals the
generating value. The statistic is twice the difference from the zero-rate
slice; formal hypothesis tests require optimizing nuisance parameters and
accounting for a null on the parameter-space boundary.

```{julia}
DataFrame(
    Comparison = ["Model 1: phi", "Model 2: phi", "Model 2: psi", "Model 3: psi"],
    GridMaximum = [
        prof.profile_eps.phi[argmax(prof.profile_eps.loglik)],
        prof.profile_phi.phi[argmax(prof.profile_phi.loglik)],
        prof.profile_psi.psi[argmax(prof.profile_psi.loglik_m2)],
        prof.profile_psi.psi[argmax(prof.profile_psi.loglik_m3)]
    ],
    TwiceLogLikelihoodDifference = [
        -2 * first(prof.profile_eps.delta_ll),
        -2 * first(prof.profile_phi.delta_ll),
        -2 * first(prof.profile_psi.delta_ll_m2),
        -2 * first(prof.profile_psi.delta_ll)
    ]
)
```

## Forward-backward Ancestral Character Estimation (`ace`)

Calling `ace(bdt, theta, dm)` runs the upward coalescent pass followed by the downward transition matrix pass (`solveQfwd0`) to compute posterior host-state probabilities `bdt.acestates` (`m × (n + Nnode)`) at every internal node of the phylogeny:

```{julia}
bdt2_ace = ace(bdt2, theta_true, zoonosis_demographic_process(model2_params());
    res = 300, timeOfOriginBoundaryCondition = false, likelihood = :PL2)

n_tips = bdt2_ace.n
int_nodes = (n_tips + 1):(n_tips + bdt2_ace.Nnode)
node_t_fwd = bdt2_ace.maxSampleTime .- bdt2_ace.heights[int_nodes]
p_human_post = bdt2_ace.acestates[2, int_nodes]
true_int_state = t2.node_state[int_nodes]

fig_ace = Figure(size = (760, 380), fontsize = 12)
ax_ace = Axis(fig_ace[1, 1];
    title = "Posterior P(Human Deme Y₂) at Internal Nodes (Model 2)",
    xlabel = "Internal node forward time t (years)",
    ylabel = "Posterior probability P(state = Y₂)"
)
idx_res = findall(==(1), true_int_state)
idx_hum = findall(==(2), true_int_state)
scatter!(ax_ace, node_t_fwd[idx_res], p_human_post[idx_res];
    color = :royalblue, markersize = 8, label = "True internal node state = Reservoir (Y₁)")
scatter!(ax_ace, node_t_fwd[idx_hum], p_human_post[idx_hum];
    color = :crimson, marker = :utriangle, markersize = 10, label = "True internal node state = Human (Y₂)")
hlines!(ax_ace, [0.5]; color = :gray50, linestyle = :dash)
axislegend(ax_ace; position = :lt, framevisible = true)
fig_ace
```

## Equilibrium island-model inference (`island_coalescent_ml`)

When demographic trajectories are unknown and demes are approximated as constant-size islands with migration rates $\mu_{kl}$ and effective population sizes $N_{e,k}$, `island_coalescent_ml`, `confint_island_coalescent`, and `boot_island_coalescent` fit the equilibrium structured coalescent model:

```{julia}
fit_island = island_coalescent_ml(t2; maxiters = 100, likelihood = :QL)
println("Fitted log-likelihood: ", round(fit_island.loglik, digits = 3))
println("Endpoint-posterior transition summary: ", round.(fit_island.expected_jumps, digits = 2))
DataFrame(
    Parameter = collect(keys(fit_island.coef)),
    Estimate = round.(collect(values(fit_island.coef)), digits = 4)
)
```

And the internal-node ancestral character table `fit_island.ace` returned by `island_coalescent_ml`:

```{julia}
first(fit_island.ace, 8)
```
